```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash

#    (the `-iname` flag makes the search case‑insensitive)
while read -r f ; do
    # Skip the directory itself so we don’t try to copy it twice
    [[ "$f" == "./backup_tests"* ]] && continue
    
    # 3️⃣ Copy each hit into the backup folder
    #     Preserve the original directory layout
    cp --parents "$f" ./backup_tests/
done < <(find . -type f -iname '*test*')
```

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `mkdir -p backup_tests` | Creates the destination folder if it doesn’t exist yet. |
| `find . -type f -iname '*test*'` | Recursively lists **files** (not dirs) whose names contain “test”, ignoring case. |
| `cp --parents …` | Copies each file while keeping its relative path intact inside `backup_tests`. |

> **Tip:** If you also want to grab directories named with “test”, replace `-type f` with `-print`.

Run the script, and you’ll end up with a clean snapshot of all “test” assets tucked away in `./backup_tests`, preserving the original folder hierarchy.
